patch_description:
The baseline uses radius_scale=1, fraction=1, memory reevaluation, and retained velocities. Its persistent interval-end errors motivate testing broader recovery after substantial deterioration.
This policy maps relative fitness drops of 2–20% to increasing response strength. It relocates 40–100% of particles, preserves more particles when the swarm already spans the response region, and expands the radius up to twice baseline. Velocity resets require severe deterioration, little recent improvement, and a compact swarm. Memory reevaluation remains enabled because its measured evaluation cost is small.
Hypothesis: partial relocation preserves useful search structure after mild changes, while broader relocation helps compact swarms recover after severe changes. Performance improvement requires evaluation.
